review_type: Independent AI editorial review of nine original A2 Lezen texts (26 closed questions) against content/reviews/rubric.md, content/blueprint.md sections 1, 3, 4.1, 5, 8, 9, 10, 12 and 13 and the Lezen A2 paragraph of docs/research/exam-blueprints-2026-09-10.md; keys proved from the verbatim evidence, distractors tested against the text, key signals scanned by script, level judged per text; small repairs applied in the proposed file per docs/briefs/review.md. The reviewer did not author the batch; the batch and the author's notes were read in that order and every verdict was checked against the batch text itself.

edits.question: q2
edits.from: Ja, maar alleen binnen 14 dagen na de koop.

edits.question: text, q2
edits.field: text ("U verdient 14,40 euro per uur." → "U verdient 15,20 euro per uur."), q2 options (14,40/15,40 → 15,20/16,20), q2 evidence, q2 explanation
edits.to: A "15,20 euro per uur en zijn reiskosten." (key) / B "15,20 euro per uur, geen reiskosten." / C "16,20 euro per uur en zijn reiskosten." / D "16,20 euro per uur, geen reiskosten."
edits.why: 14,40 is the statutory minimum hourly wage of 1 July 2025; from 1 January 2026 the adult (21+) minimum is 14,71 and from 1 July 2026 14,99 (rijksoverheid.nl, checked 2026-09-10), so the advertised wage would be below the legal minimum in the year of the text (open morning zaterdag 6 juni 2026), against blueprint section 8. The arithmetic of q2 is unchanged in shape.

items.level_reason: 182 words, prose average 6.3, longest 11; the register of a shop's house rules (question-then-dan conditions, imperatives). Three rule applications: 21 days between the 14- and 30-day thresholds, an exclusion that overrides the price-tag condition, a refund delay against the return deadlines. Like the official company-rules text.
items.evidence: q1 B from "Brengt u het kledingstuk na 14 dagen terug? Dan krijgt u geen geld terug. U kunt het kledingstuk wel ruilen. Of u krijgt een tegoedbon."; three weeks is after 14 and before 30 days ("Na 30 dagen nemen wij niets meer terug"); A is the within-14-days rule, C the after-30-days rule. q2 C from "Ondergoed, sokken en zwemkleding nemen wij nooit terug. Ook niet met prijskaartje."; A applies the tag condition that the same sentence overrides; B (edited) claims an exchange limit of 14 days, contradicted by "U kunt het kledingstuk wel ruilen" after 14 days. q3 B from "Het geld staat binnen vijf werkdagen op uw rekening." (one week is within 14 days, so the refund applies); A reads "Dan krijgt u uw geld terug" as at the till, C and D are the return deadlines.

items.level_reason: 156 words with a four-row hours table; q1 combines the Thursday row with the after-18.00 rule, q2 the Saturday closing time with the return box, q3 is a one-line reason lookup. Domain opleiding accepted.

Boeken lenen kan dan alleen bij de automaat."; B the desk is closed after 18.00, C the library is open until 20.00. q2 C from "Wilt u boeken inleveren? Gebruik dan de brievenbus naast de ingang. Dat kan dag en nacht, ook als de bibliotheek dicht is."; A 18.00 is the Mon/Wed/Fri time, Saturday closes at 16.00; B "zondag – gesloten". q3 D from "Veel mensen willen 's avonds komen om te leren en te lezen. Daarom zijn wij op dinsdag en donderdag langer open."; A reversed (no staff after 18.00), B a table fact with no causal link, C the Taalcafé is Wednesday 10.30–12.00.

diversity_review: Nine distinct settings covering all eight A2 reading task types (bericht twice) and five of the eight domains (winkels-diensten, opleiding, wonen-buurt, vrije-tijd-familie ×2 each, werk ×1; gezondheid, instanties and vervoer are covered by the sibling batch 020). No slug reuse against the catalogue or batches 001–020 and no re-skin of an existing item; tested operations vary (threshold rules, table plus after-hours rule, deadline with alternative, dated instructions in an e-mail, schedule against working hours with a holiday exception and a price sum, two-job choice with a 2×2 pay rule, temporary relocation with cause, rota plus house number, membership rule with an exemption). Nearest neighbours: gezinskaart and zwemrooster share the age-band price structure and the sentence "Kinderen tot en met 3 jaar: gratis" (also close to batch004-stadsbus); ketel and batch004-verwarming both concern the cv-ketel of a housing corporation (planned check vs failure card); schoonmaker is the third job advertisement (different structure from batch004-magazijn and p4); openingstijden and batch020-politiebureau are both opening-hours texts; dierentuin and the listening item batch001-schoolreis share the school-trip setting across parts. Personas: Fatima in five texts (1, 2, 4, 5, 9), Karim in five (3, 5, 6, 7, 9), Roos in four; Fatima's children (a son in 1, Amina 10 in 4 and 9, a daughter of 3 and a son of 8 in 5) and Karim's four children in 9 are not contradictory but forms should not place these texts consecutively.
set_assembly: Balanced drills of three texts (keys within 20–40% per letter, near neighbours apart): A = terugbrengen + openingstijden + schoonmaker (regels, bericht, advertentie; 9 Q, keys A2 B3 C3 D1); B = ketel + weekmarkt + gezinskaart (brief, krant, folder; 8 Q, A3 B2 C2 D1; Karim appears in all three); C = dierentuin + zwemrooster + trappenhuis (email, rooster, bericht; 9 Q, A2 B3 C3 D1). Do not put zwemrooster and gezinskaart, or ketel and batch004-verwarming, in one drill. A mock form needs about ten texts and 25 questions: this batch supplies nine texts and 26 questions on its own; with 020 (nine texts, 23 questions) and 004 (twelve texts, 30 questions) two forms without shared items are possible, but each form must be re-checked for key balance (the checker fails an unbalanced form) and for the yes/no polarity pattern: 020 has three yes/no questions whose key is the odd polarity out (identiteitskaart q1 and q2, spoorwerk q2), so a form should not stack them with the three balanced ones here. No picture-answer item exists yet in 004, 020 or 021; the launch bank still needs one (blueprint 4.1).
media_notes: Reading items: no audio, no pictures. Three texts carry a plain-text table with " – " separated rows (openingstijden, zwemrooster, gezinskaart), rendered by the app with white-space: pre-line as in batch 004; the checker's six sentence-length warnings come from those rows and the letter/e-mail headers merging with the next sentence and are known artefacts.
observations_not_blocking: zwemrooster writes the activity labels "Banen zwemmen" and "Vrij zwemmen" as two words; the one-word compounds are also common on pool boards; left as written because both forms are in wide use and the two-word form is more transparent at A2.

weekmarkt q2 (purpose) has its gist in the headline "Zaterdagmarkt verhuist naar het Stationsplein", like the adopted batch004-ramen item; the key still needs "een half jaar" and the paraphrase "ergens anders", and the three distractors are each contradicted by the body.
Three keys are the shortest option by one word (ketel q2, zwemrooster q2, weekmarkt q3), never by characters; not a usable signal.

limitations: AI editorial review of original practice material; difficulty labels remain unvalidated authoring targets and no official approval, scoring or exam equivalence is claimed. The level column compares each text with the official description and with the calibrated batch 004, not with a teacher rating or learner data; content/exemplars/ does not exist yet.
